description: Create a post on X/Twitter, Bluesky, LinkedIn, Mastodon or Telegram (Threads, Instagram and Facebook coming soon) with optional media. Posts immediately or at a scheduled time. Publish to several accounts at once by naming account_ids instead of account_id, and give one of them its own text or media with account_configurations. Note: Instagram REQUIRES media. X posts whose text contains a link are billed at $0.25 each on paid plans and are rejected on the Free plan (x_link_posts_require_paid_plan); X accounts connected with your own X API keys are exempt. A spent monthly post or scheduled-post quota answers 429 usage_limit_exceeded, which waiting does not clear; the separate per-minute burst limit on the API key answers 429 rate_limited and does clear. Set draft: true to save the post without sending it: nothing reaches the platform, nothing counts against the monthly quota, the text may even be empty, and the answer carries a `warnings` array saying per account what would go wrong if it were sent as it stands. chirpie_update_post edits a draft and promotes it with schedule_at or publish: true.

configuration.description: Publishing options for this account only, instead of the shared ones. The whole block is replaced rather than merged, so an account publishing as a reel while the rest go to the feed carries its own instagram block.

facebook.description: How a Facebook Page (coming soon) publishes this post.

link.description: A URL to attach to a feed post, shown as a link preview. Feed posts only.

placement.description: Where the post goes on the Page: feed (the default), or story, which takes exactly one image or video, no text and no first comment.

instagram.description: How an Instagram account (coming soon) publishes this post. A story carries no caption (send empty text), no first comment and no collaborators. A reel takes one video, collaborators, user tags, a cover, share_to_feed and trial_reel.

collaborators.description: Up to 3 Instagram usernames to invite as co-authors, without the @. The post appears on a collaborator's profile once they accept the invitation, which happens on Instagram. Feed posts and reels only.

cover.description: The id of an uploaded image to use as a reel's cover. Use this or video_cover_timestamp_ms, never both: Instagram reads the image and ignores the timestamp, so sending both would drop one of the two things you asked for.

placement.description: Where the post goes: feed (the default) takes up to 10 images, story takes exactly one image or video, reel takes exactly one video and no images.

share_to_feed.description: Whether a reel also appears on the profile grid.

trial_reel.description: Publish as a trial reel, shown to people who do not follow the account first. Reels only.

graduation.description: How the reel reaches the account's followers: 'manual' waits for the customer to release it, 'performance' releases it once Instagram decides it is doing well.

user_tags.description: The people to tag. A feed post needs both x and y on every tag, a story may carry both or neither, and a reel takes the username on its own, because Instagram reads coordinates only on images and stories. Tags belong to one image, so a carousel carrying them is refused.

x.description: Distance from the left edge, 0 to 1.

y.description: Distance from the top edge, 0 to 1.

video_cover_timestamp_ms.description: A frame of the reel itself to use as its cover, in milliseconds.

first_comment.description: A first comment for this account only, instead of the shared one. An empty string publishes this account with no first comment at all, which is how a fan-out sends one to the accounts that take a first comment while an account that does not still publishes the post. Leave it out and the account inherits the shared one.

media.description: Media for this account only, replacing the shared media. An empty array publishes this account with no media.

alt.description: A description of the item, for people using a screen reader.

id.description: The id chirpie_upload_media returned. Valid for 7 days.

url.description: A public image or video URL for Chirpie to fetch.

media_ids.description: Ids from chirpie_upload_media, for this account only.

media_urls.description: Public image or video URLs for this account only.

text.description: Text for this account only, instead of the shared text.

account_configurations.description: Per-account overrides, keyed by account ID. Every key must also be in account_ids. An account with no entry publishes the shared text and media. Media never merges: an account naming any media field replaces the shared media outright. Use one media spelling at a time.

account_id.description: Account ID to post from (X, Bluesky, LinkedIn, Mastodon or Telegram; Threads, Instagram and Facebook coming soon). Use this or account_ids, not both.

account_ids.description: Account IDs to publish the same post to, 1 to 25 of them, each named once. Naming this instead of account_id answers with a group_id and one result per account, in the order given, each with its own `success`: an account whose platform refused is reported there while the others stay published. Anything that fails the request as a whole (a character limit, a media rule, a spent quota) publishes nothing.

configuration.description: Per-platform publishing options, keyed by platform. Two platforms take options, both coming soon: Instagram takes a feed post, a story or a reel, and a Facebook Page takes a feed post or a story; leave it out and everything publishes to the feed. Nothing is dropped quietly: a block keyed on a platform that takes no options, on a platform no account in the call uses, or a field the chosen placement does not carry, is refused with 400 configuration_unsupported naming the platform and the field. One block serves every account of that platform; give one account its own with an account_configurations entry.

cover.description: The id of an uploaded image to use as a reel's cover. Use this or video_cover_timestamp_ms, never both: Instagram reads the image and ignores the timestamp, so sending both would drop one of the two things you asked for.

placement.description: Where the post goes: feed (the default) takes up to 10 images, story takes exactly one image or video, reel takes exactly one video and no images.

trial_reel.description: Publish as a trial reel, shown to people who do not follow the account first. Reels only.

graduation.description: How the reel reaches the account's followers: 'manual' waits for the customer to release it, 'performance' releases it once Instagram decides it is doing well.

x.description: Distance from the left edge, 0 to 1.

y.description: Distance from the top edge, 0 to 1.

video_cover_timestamp_ms.description: A frame of the reel itself to use as its cover, in milliseconds.

draft.description: Save the post without sending it. It is stored with status draft, nothing reaches the platform, and it costs no quota. The answer carries a `warnings` array naming, per account, anything that would stop it publishing as it stands.

first_comment.description: A comment to publish under the post the moment it goes out, the "link in the first comment" pattern. Available on X, and on Threads, Instagram and Facebook (coming soon). Sending it to any other platform is refused with 400 first_comment_unsupported rather than dropped, and on a fan-out that refuses the whole request; an account_configurations entry whose first_comment is an empty string opts one account out. It counts as one post against the monthly quota, like a reply, and on X a first comment containing a link carries the same $0.25 surcharge a link post does and is rejected on the Free plan. It never fails the post: if it cannot be posted the post is still published and the answer carries first_comment with status "failed" and a reason, which chirpie_retry_first_comment sends again.

idempotency_key.description: A key of your own making that makes retrying this call safe. The same key with the same request replays the first answer for 24 hours instead of sending it again; the same key with a different request is refused with 422 idempotency_key_reused, and a retry that arrives while the first is still running is refused with 409 idempotency_in_progress; a retry after the first has finished collects the replay.

media.description: Uploaded files and public links, each with optional alt text. An entry takes either `id`, from chirpie_upload_media, or `url`, a public link Chirpie fetches. `alt` describes the item for people using a screen reader and is carried to X, Bluesky, LinkedIn and Mastodon, and to Instagram and Facebook (coming soon). Use this or media_urls, not both. Images per post: X 4, Bluesky 4 (977 KB each), LinkedIn 4 (JPEG, PNG, GIF up to 8 MB), Mastodon 4, Telegram 10, and once available Threads 1, Instagram 10 (carousel), Facebook 10. Video: X, Mastodon and Telegram only, one per post and never alongside images. Instagram REQUIRES at least 1 image. Anything a platform cannot take is refused with 400 unsupported_media, never dropped.

alt.description: A description of the item, for people using a screen reader.

id.description: The id chirpie_upload_media returned. Valid for 7 days.

url.description: A public image or video URL for Chirpie to fetch.

media_ids.description: Ids from chirpie_upload_media, for a post that needs no alt text. Same per-platform rules as `media`. Use one of media, media_ids or media_urls, not several.

media_urls.description: Public image or video URLs, for a post that needs no alt text. Same per-platform rules as `media`.

schedule_at.description: ISO 8601 datetime to schedule the post. Either an absolute instant carrying a timezone, such as '2026-04-01T14:00:00Z' or '2026-04-01T16:00:00+02:00', or a local time with no offset, such as '2026-11-01T09:30:00', which is read in the timezone parameter or the one saved on the account and is refused when there is neither. Scheduled posts publish within ~5 minutes of this time. On a draft it is only the time you have in mind: the post is not queued for it.

text.description: Post text, and what an account with no override of its own publishes (max 280 chars for standard X, 25,000 for X Premium, 300 for Bluesky, 3,000 for LinkedIn, 500 for Mastodon, 4,096 for Telegram, or 1,024 for Telegram when media_urls is set; coming soon: 500 for Threads, 2,200 for Instagram, 63,206 for Facebook)

timezone.description: The IANA timezone a schedule_at with no offset is read in, such as 'America/New_York'. Daylight saving is worked out for the date named, which is what makes '09:30 on 1 November' come out right. Ignored when schedule_at already carries an offset. Leave it out to use the timezone saved on the account.
